newsitem.title: USA: NY utilities file ISO transmission rules with FERC.
newsitem.headline: NY utilities file ISO transmission rules with FERC.

text.p: New York's nine electric utilities filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Friday their initial transmission rules for a proposed Independent System Operator (ISO) as the state's electric market begins to deregulate in 1998.
An ISO is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the state's bulk power system.

"The rules filed today would help ensure that ISO adheres to well established and sound engineering practice in its operation of the bulk power system," the New York Power Pool (NYPP) said in a statement.

The New York State Public Service Commission, the agency responsible for overseeing the provision of electricity service in the state, expressed concern that pressures from commercial interest in a competitive market could erode the level of electric service reliability, NYPP said.
These initial rules would be adopted by the New York State Reliability Council, which would ensure the reliability of the state's electricity service in a competitive environment, NYPP said.

NYPP is a utility consortium that includes Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Long Island Lighting Co, New York Power Authority, New York State Electric & Gas Corp, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, Orange and Rockland Utilities and Rochester Gas and Electric Corp.
